items.reviewNote: Ah marks the giant’s indignation in unit 179 and the secretary’s recognition of a suspicion in unit 215. The published ah emotional sense and its three joyful-discovery questions were read. Add broader reaction questions on the existing interjection meaning, not separate outrage and recognition meanings. The four alternatives are grammatical interjection labels; physical pain, a hush request and water noise are explicitly excluded by the clue.

Avec indignation, avec confiance and avec beaucoup de bonté name the state or manner accompanying speech. The published broad with preposition and its three accompaniment/instrument questions were read. Add a manner bank on that same French preposition meaning, not three emotion-only meanings. The four alternatives fit confidence as a complement; positive manner rather than absence, concession or time selects avec.

Concevoir asks whether one can imagine this extreme madness, matching the earlier I concevons_imagine plan and V concevez bridge. The whole earlier meaning and three-band bank were read; the infinitive shares the same proper planned French verb meaning, not biological conception. All four infinitives fit cette chose as a direct object; mental representation selects concevoir, and conjugation alone does not create a sense.

Forcenée qualifies rage as frenzied and unrestrained. No global or earlier French forcené family exists. All four adjectives agree with feminine singular rage; frenzy contrasts with calm, moderation and gentleness. The bank records the giant’s rhetoric and does not infer a clinical condition or literal loss of mental faculties.

Il me prend envie uses impersonal prendre for the onset of a desire in someone, not a wind gaining strength or taking an object by hand. The global prendre family and all earlier acquisition, capture, action and measuring proposals were read. Prepare this onset-of-feeling meaning under the existing French verb lemma and share later prit fantaisie when reviewed. The four choices are grammatical verb labels in the unchanged metalinguistic prompt; sudden arising distinguishes prend from passing, lack or persistence.

Trois coups de pied are three blows or kicks, not clock sounds, a sudden-event phrase or legal exposure. The published coup physical-blow meaning and its complete bank were inspected. Add the plural surface to that same French noun meaning, not a number-only sense. Coups/saluts/regards/sourires are masculine plural nouns; striking rather than greeting, looking or smiling selects coups.

Assassins names the combatants as intentional killers under the giant’s condemnation, not persons merely accused or an adjective modifying another noun. No global or earlier French assassin family exists. Assassins/sauveteurs/témoins/protecteurs are masculine plural nouns; intentional killing rather than rescue, observation or protection selects assassins. The source judgment is attributed to the character, not asserted as a legal finding.

Ridicules qualifies assassins as absurd objects of derision under the giant’s judgment. The published ridicule adjective and all three questions were inspected. Add the plural surface on the same absurdity meaning, not the nominal ridicule sense or a plural-only identity. All four predicates agree masculine plural; absurdity selects ridicules without endorsing the character’s proposed killing.

Travaillent à leur ruine describes activity contributing to their own destruction, ironically making the giant’s intervention unnecessary. The existing effort/activity definition and earlier V travaillaient bridge were read; this is not psychological torment of someone else. Add the present plural surface to that existing French verb meaning, not a self-destruction-only sense. Each plural predicate fits the unchanged subject ils; effort rather than rest, waiting or sleeping selects travaillent.

Leur ruine is the people’s destruction or downfall, not a surviving architectural ruin or strictly a financial bankruptcy. No global or earlier French ruine family exists. Ruine/prospérité/paix/sécurité are feminine singular nouns in the unchanged leur slot. Destruction rather than flourishing, peace or safety selects ruine, with future conceptual overlap recorded for final whole-work reconciliation.

Both Sachez introduce factual claims the philosopher wants the giants to know, not instructions to know how to perform a skill. The proper published knowledge definition and II savez/savaient targets were read. Add the imperative surface on that same knowledge meaning; grammatical mood alone does not create a fresh sense. All four imperatives fit ceci and select awareness over forgetting, concealing or denying; casualty assertions remain source claims.

La centième partie expresses a one-hundredth fraction of the soldiers, not a claim verified from historical records. No global or earlier French centième family exists. The four ordinal adjectives agree with feminine singular partie; the explicit denominator one hundred selects centième rather than ten, a thousand or two. This bank is an adjective, not a noun-number-only meaning.

Ces misérables names the unfortunate soldiers rather than modifying a following noun. The global misérable family and the VI adjective pitiable bank were read; no proper noun owner exists. Prepare proper nominal ownership and the pitiable-person meaning, preserving the earlier adjective identity. Misérables/privilégiés/vainqueurs/heureux are masculine plural substantive nouns; suffering and pity select misérables rather than advantage, victory or happiness.

Quand même ils n’auraient pas tiré l’épée is a hypothetical completed action with avoir as compound auxiliary, not ownership of a weapon or voice organs. The earlier VI lexical auraient bank was read and excluded. Share the proper published compound-auxiliary sense already used by VI a/avaient/avoir, adding this conditional surface without a tense-only meaning. Middle alternatives are grammatical verb labels; the explicit auxiliary role selects auraient.

Tiré l’épée means drawing a sword from its sheath, and by context entering combat. The existing take-out tirer definition and three questions were read; the earlier IV straight-line tiré au cordeau bank is different. Add this participial surface on the same draw-out meaning, not a line-drawing, shooting or weapon-only sense. Each participle fits son épée; taking out rather than concealment, damage or dropping selects tiré.

L’épée is the conventional sword that soldiers would draw, not evidence of a particular battlefield weapon model. No global or earlier French épée family exists. Épée/lance/hache/massue are feminine singular nouns and all fit une. The handle and long straight two-edged blade distinguish the sword from a shaft with a point, an axe head or a club, without using gender or number to eliminate alternatives.

Fatigue names the soldiers’ physical exhaustion as one cause of death, not wear of a mechanical component. No global or earlier French fatigue family exists. Fatigue/détente/vigueur/vitalité are feminine singular nouns, all fitting la; exhaustion rather than relaxation, strength or energy selects fatigue. The causal claim remains attributed to the philosopher rather than treated as a verified mortality estimate.

Intempérance names excess and lack of restraint among the soldiers’ self-destructive causes, especially in drinking or eating. No global or earlier French intempérance family exists. Intempérance/tempérance/prudence/sobriété are feminine singular noun labels in a metalinguistic prompt, avoiding an l’ elision filter. Lack of moderation rather than restraint, caution or sobriety selects intempérance; no clinical diagnosis or particular individual is inferred.

La faim, la fatigue ou l’intempérance les emportent means that these causes carry the soldiers off in death. Académie 1762 records the disease-causes-death construction. The global emporter transport, victory and physical-destruction meanings and all their questions were read; prepare the death-causing meaning under the existing French verb lemma, comparing metaphorical-destruction overlap before import. Each plural verb fits les; death rather than healing, protection or sparing selects emportent.

Punir concerns whom to punish for the massacres, without prescribing a real-world legal action. The proper published punir family contains redundant tense-labeled meanings; the past bank’s semantic penalty definition and all three questions were read. Share that existing punishment meaning rather than inventing a fresh infinitive-only sense. Before import, full current/historical family impact review must normalize its participle-only wording and reconcile future/present duplicates while preserving unchanged legacy mastery. All four infinitives take cet individu; a penalty rather than reward, excuse or praise selects punir.

Ces barbares names the rulers as cruel people ordering distant deaths, not foreign-language speakers or a historical ethnic group. No global or earlier French barbare family exists. Prepare a proper noun owner for the cruel-person meaning. Barbares/bienfaiteurs/protecteurs/sauveurs are masculine plural nouns; cruelty rather than beneficence, protection or rescue selects barbares. The moral judgment is the philosopher’s, not an externally verified classification.

Sédentaires describes the rulers who remain in their offices while others fight, not a medical claim about their exercise habits. No global or earlier French sédentaire family exists. All four adjective predicates agree masculine plural; staying rather than nomadism, travel or wandering selects sédentaires. It modifies barbares and does not create a second nominal owner.

Du fond de leur cabinet places the rulers at the remote interior of a room. The published fond definition includes the deepest or essential part, but its existing bank tests the heart of an issue. Add a physical-depth bank on that same broad noun sense; other source uses retain essential and inner-heart contexts. Fond/vestibule/seuil/plafond are masculine singular nouns in le, with remoteness from the entrance rather than entry space, threshold or overhead surface selecting fond.

Dans le fond du cœur locates the giant’s displeasure in his innermost feelings, not at an anatomical measurable depth. Share the published deepest/essential-part fond meaning, as with the physical room and essential philosophical matter. All middle choices fond/bord/contour/dessus are masculine singular noun labels; inner depth rather than boundary, outline or upper surface selects fond. No heart-anatomy or emotion-specific new meaning is made.

Leur cabinet is the rulers’ private working room, not the staff assisting a minister. The exact surface staff bank and the global private-study meaning with all three questions were read. Add the contextual surface bank to the existing study sense, preserving staff mastery. Cabinet/vestibule/couloir/salon are masculine singular nouns after un; a secluded study differs from an entry hall, passage or reception room.

Ordonnent describes rulers issuing orders for massacres, not arranging objects in a sequence or granting a medical prescription. No global or earlier French ordonner family exists. All four plural predicates begin with vowels and fit l’, avoiding an elision eliminator; command rather than prohibition, prevention or avoidance selects ordonnent. The bank describes speech authority without authorizing actual violence.

Dans le temps de leur digestion describes rulers ordering deaths while digesting their meals. No global or earlier French digestion family exists. Digestion/respiration/marche/réflexion are feminine singular nouns after la; processing food differs from breathing, walking or thinking. The satirical contrast does not become a medical claim about a named person.

Le massacre d’un million d’hommes names the collective killing ordered by rulers. The existing massacrer verb cannot own this noun, and no global or earlier proper massacre noun exists. Massacre/sauvetage/pardon/refuge are masculine singular nouns after un; brutal killing differs from rescue, forgiveness or shelter. The source’s quantity remains a narrative claim, not a verified casualty figure.

Un million d’hommes expresses one thousand thousands as a noun followed by de. The earlier I millions_number proper noun plan and its complete bank were read. Add the singular surface on that same cardinal-group meaning, not a singular-only new sense. Million/millier/milliard/billion are masculine singular number-group nouns in the arithmetic frame; the stated product selects million rather than a different numerical group. The number is a source assertion, not independently confirmed history.

Solennellement describes official ceremonial thanks to God ordered after a massacre, creating an ironic moral contrast. No global or earlier French solennellement family exists. All four adverbs fit agissent; ceremony differs from informality, secrecy or gaiety. The bank explains the manner without treating the ceremony as morally justified or adding a religious-only meaning.

Ému de pitié describes the giant emotionally moved by compassion, not a body physically shaken or a popular disturbance. No global or earlier French émouvoir family exists. Prepare the emotional-movement meaning under the proper verb lemma; the participial surface does not create a second adjectival lemma by default. All four masculine singular predicates fit il est; being touched differs from indifference, insensitivity or boredom.

La petite race humaine denotes all humankind, as explicitly recorded by Académie, rather than ancestry of one family or a subdivision of humans. The global proper race noun’s lineage and figurative kinds meanings with all their banks were read. Prepare the humankind-in-race-humaine context on that same noun lemma; before import compare the scope of figurative kind/group without conflating it with family ancestry. Race/lignée/famille/tribu are feminine singular nouns agreeing with humaine; the explicit entire-humanity rather than lineage/subgroup clue selects race.

Il découvrait des contrastes means finding or perceiving differences in humans that the giant did not know, not removing a cover from a pot. The global finding/learning meaning and its complete bank were read; the VI revealing-to-another proposal is a different causal perspective. Add this imperfect surface on the existing discover/find meaning, with no contrast-only or tense-only sense. Each singular predicate fits les; discovery differs from ignorance, denial or concealment.

Étonnants qualifies surprising contrasts in humanity. The existing proper étonnant adjective and the earlier V étonnante bridge were read in all three bands. Add this masculine plural surface to the same surprise meaning, preserving feminine singular mastery and avoiding a gender/number-only sense. All four predicates agree masculine plural; surprise differs from the ordinary, expected or familiar.

Contrastes names marked opposing traits: human intellectual capacity and violent self-destruction. No global or earlier French contraste family exists. Contrastes/accords/liens/rapprochements are masculine plural nouns in des; opposition rather than accord, connection or rapprochement selects contrastes. No exclusively visual/light-dark sense or difference-only new lemma is inferred.

Vous ne tuez personne assumes these sages do not kill for money. The exact VII tuent bank and its three questions were read; tuez shares that planned killing meaning under the same proper French tuer verb lemma, not a second-person-only sense. Every verb fits les and the unchanged vous subject; death rather than injury, rescue or fear selects tuez. The neutral retrieval paraphrase does not accuse the source sages of killing.

Both dites-moi ask the interlocutors to tell the giant their occupation or explain soul and ideas. The published dire speech meaning and earlier IV dites bank were read. The token includes the hyphenated indirect-object moi; retain this exact source surface on the existing French verb meaning, without a pronoun-combination-only fresh sense. All four imperative compounds take cette réponse; explicit spoken communication rather than hiding, showing or writing selects dites-moi.

The two c’est de quoi clauses resume previously stated philosophical propositions as things about which the speaker doubts or does not doubt. The exact interrogative quoi bank and VI exclamative quoi bank were read and excluded for these relative contexts. The global generic thing-as-object quoi definition supports the same what/thing reference in a relative construction: add a contextual bank there rather than a relative-function-only new meaning. All alternatives are grammatical word labels in a metalinguistic prompt; thing reference differs from person, place and time. The unit 185 question retains interrogative quoi.

À quoi vous vous occupez asks what activity the sages pursue, answered by dissection, measurement and arithmetic. No global or earlier French occuper verb family exists. Prepare the pronominal activity meaning under the proper French occuper lemma; historical à complement in the source is recorded, while the independent middle paraphrase uses standard de. All four second-person plural pronominal predicates take de cette activité; active engagement rather than memory, avoidance or distrust selects occupez.

The philosopher adds that the remote rulers, rather than the soldiers alone, deserve punishment. The VI full-span bank and its published component identity were inspected and reused unchanged. This is an additional argument, not spatial elsewhere; final import must retain the published meaning with no duplicate component mastery. Newly considered component forms in VII package02 reuse this exact full-span bank; all three earlier questions were re-read unchanged, and no new expression meaning or duplicated component mastery is created.

Point du tout and rien du tout reinforce a complete negation, concerning understanding and action respectively. They are not the quantity pronoun tout standing for everything. All adverbs fit the negative completion while absolute exclusion alone selects du tout; each complete source span is retained to suppress duplicate component mastery. Newly considered component forms in VII package02 reuse this exact full-span bank; all three earlier questions were re-read unchanged, and no new expression meaning or duplicated component mastery is created.

The Sirian politely requests an account of the sages’ activities. This source formula is an entreaty, not the response to thanks that identical words can express elsewhere. Each first-person clause fits the quotation; polite requesting rather than prohibition, reproach or congratulation selects it. Je/vous/en/prie components stay within this specific formula. Newly considered component forms in VII package02 reuse this exact full-span bank; all three earlier questions were re-read unchanged, and no new expression meaning or duplicated component mastery is created.

The unit 182 ten-year period ends with few soldiers surviving. The complete Chapter I temporal au_bout_de bank and all three questions were read unchanged; duration rather than spatial endpoint selects this full phrase. Suppress its current au/bout components at import while preserving that earlier full-expression meaning.

Au moins sets a minimal question about whether the speaker knows matter at all, rather than a maximum or merely chronological condition. The earlier V minimum phrase bank and its three questions were read unchanged; preserve its meaning and suppress the new au component on this complete source span.

Quand même with conditional auraient introduces a concessive counterfactual hypothesis: even without combat, other causes would kill them. It is not literal temporal when or independent even. All four subordinate connectors fit a clause prompt as grammatical labels; concession regardless of the hypothesis differs from cause, condition or time. Prepare one full-span expression bank and suppress both components before import.

The philosopher tells the giant not to make the effort to destroy humans, since they already bring about their own ruin. The full negative source phrase realizes se donner la peine, not literal giving, sorrow or punishment. Share the existing effort noun meaning through a proper complete-expression bridge before import; negation does not create a second canonical positive/negative meaning. All four full imperative alternatives fit a metalinguistic sentence prompt and the effort clue selects the target. Earlier-package ne/vous/en/pas component routes must be suppressed on this exact span, without altering their other uses or mastery.

The giant says the supposed prenatal knowledge was not worth the trouble if the soul becomes ignorant later. This is an evaluation of usefulness, not sorrow or a penal sentence; prepare the canonical être la peine/valoir la peine worth-the-trouble meaning with the negative occurrence recorded exactly. No negative-only fresh meaning or claim that prenatal knowledge actually exists is made. Every full predicate fits cela; useless effort selects the target. Suppress exact earlier component word routes before import.

The promised philosophy book would reveal final understanding of reality, while its eventual blankness makes that promise ironic. Le bout des choses denotes ultimate explanation, not a physical extremity. Prepare the complete phrase under a proper expression owner and compare its conceptual endpoint overlap with the broad published bout before import. All four masculine singular complete noun phrases fit verraient; knowledge rather than spatial edges, room location or elapsed time selects the target. Earlier des/choses word routes must be suppressed on this exact span before import.

reviewBasis: Full source thought units, independently written meaning clues, every middle alternative, noun number and agreement, distinct meanings and explicit ownership dependencies were individually inspected. Structural checks verify revision and coverage, never editorial approval.
